pullRequest.body:
Gallery 2 replaces the 278 placeholder layouts with 28 OPF 0.19 intent templates and publishes schema 2. This is a major release: six reused IDs have new template semantics, other removed IDs have no aliases, and previews now provide one SVG per layout. Narrative beats reference the new templates; their prose and unrelated catalog kinds remain unchanged.

The first schema-2 release must precede the final core 0.19 registry release. Its one-release bootstrap now pins actual merged core `00022a4ed3d2576bd09c003aa38659ed5d014bc5` and renderer `0e18fb532736248ff7c96a2a3c05cbf32a86b68c`. It verifies default-branch ancestry, builds frozen sources, and stages gallery/core/renderer development artifacts with unchanged own versions and runtime bytes. Exact original/staged manifests, file inventories, and shared core/gallery resolution are verified. The published gallery remains dependency-free; its release manifest, lockfile and catalog bytes are unchanged by bootstrap. CI retains the hidden identity evidence in a narrowly scoped artifact upload.

The 2.0.0 changelog and contributor instructions describe the breaking catalog/preview contracts and the three-artifact bootstrap. After the engine releases, ordinary registry development pins replace this bootstrap in a separate change.

Validation on a fresh, clean checkout of `1c7ccd34f51e82de63afd67c5de14a06136e599c`, Node 24.21.0 and npm 11.16.0:

- `npm ci` and the full merged-source bootstrap passed.
- License and catalog verification passed; 78 tests and TypeScript checks passed.
- All 28 committed previews match; major-version pixel stability and pack dry run passed.
- Final strict bootstrap verification passed. Supervisor independently verified the release manifest/lock hashes and all 313 installed artifact files across the three packages.

Hosted checks and the merged release commit remain required before the `v2.0.0` tag triggers trusted publishing. Registry provenance verification follows publication. These results do not claim native Office acceptance or publication of the engine packages.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Major breaking layout catalog and preview contract for all OPF 0.19 consumers, plus one-off CI bootstrap that installs pinned engine sources from git instead of npm.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Gallery 2.0.0** is a major catalog release for OPF 0.19: it drops the 278 `opf-layout/v1` placeholder layouts in favor of **28 intent-named `opf-layout/v2` grid templates**, bumps **`CATALOG_SCHEMA` to 2**, and requires **`@openpresentation/opf` 0.19+**. Six ids (`agenda`, `comparison`, `dashboard`, `faq`, `timeline`, `two-column`) keep their names but new semantics; other 1.x layout ids are removed with no aliases.
> 
> The **preview contract** changes from many HTML thumbnails to **one renderer-drawn SVG per layout**, with `npm run check:previews` enforced in CI alongside updated stability rules for schema 2.
> 
> **Contributing and ownership** shift: v2 layouts are edited in `catalog/layouts/` here (index entries gain `summary`/`group`); pptx.gallery sync for layouts is retired.
> 
> For this release only, **`.github/bootstrap-engines.json`** and **`scripts/bootstrap-engines.mjs`** pin merged **core** and **opf-render** commits, stage local tarballs for gates before those packages hit npm, **`--verify`** locks engine/gallery identity, and workflows upload bootstrap evidence artifacts (timeouts extended to 30 minutes).
>
